chapter: Bird's world, singers and the new music
title: Philadelphia Downbeat Club: Bird, Dizzy and Gene Ammons
summary: Bird dominated for him; Dizzy envied Bird's ease; he met Jug Ammons at the Downbeat.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: What do you remember specifically (we have talked about this a little bit) about the Philadelphia days, and the Downbeat club and that whole period?

Well, in that area... See, this is funny, because Bird was over in Philly at the same time I was over there. He really so much to say, that I couldn't see any farther than what Bird was doing -- although they had cats who could play. Like, they had a tenor player there who played pretty good, but I can't think of his name. And Red Rodney was around, and there were some other people around. But Bird was so dominant a force that I didn't have time to listen to nobody else. I would listen to Bird!
And this thing was about Dizzy, I guess, because Dizzy

was trying to do the same thing... He used to get mad at Bird, because Bird played so relaxed and so free and so easy. Dizzy was apt to say, "Listen to that motherfucker." I'd say, "I hear him. You don't have to tell me to listen to him. What you gonna do about it?" He said, "Well, we've got to figure out some way." I'd say, "How you gonna do it? Just tell me how you're gonna do it." (?) in the first place, because man, how could you outdo Bird? Bird was way ahead of everybody -- I think anyway.
Because you told me that they were playing there with Hines, and that's when you met them.
Yeah. Well, that's when I really got to know Bird. Like, I played at the Downbeat for... Was that the name of the joint?

Nat Segal had it. Yeah, it's been a long time. I had to stop and think whether that was the club. So many "Downbeat's" have been by. They had one here in New York and they had one in Chicago, I think -- that's two places they had a Downbeat.
Yeah. Because I remember Gene Ammons was playing in the Downbeat Club out in Chicago; and that's how I got to know him, through the Downbeat Club. He was

playing... Now, he was another one. He had his own thing going, too, you know.. When you're talking about the way different guys can play and how they can get around their music. That had nothing to do with anyone else's thing, except that Jug had... I guess maybe he learned a lot from his father. But he had his own thing that was definitely set.
